title: Returns tote
use_case: Warehouse returns: a plastic tote (300 x 200 mm, 120 mm tall) stands on the packing bench with its hinged lid shut; the lid overhangs the tote by a 15 mm lip all round. Open the lid, put a small rigid carton (about 120 x 80 x 60 mm, 300 g) and a flat shrink-wrapped pack (about 150 x 100 x 20 mm, 150 g) from the bench into the tote, then close the lid.
headline: A single tool completes the task in 8 of 8 runs.

candidates.rating: rated 4.15 kg on a smooth face (holding force over a 1.5 safety factor)
candidates.caveat: Vacuum area frame (approximation): the cups of the suction cup model on a rigid frame, each with its own seal test and its own vacuum valve (a cup that does not seal stays off). The holding force is the sum of the sealed cups' caps; the payload is that force over a safety factor (1.5 smooth, 2.0 porous, 2.5 swivelling, all [assumed]) at 1 g. Only the smooth rating is a simulated claim: the porous and swivelling ratings are arithmetic on the same force, because no leak, porosity or swivel is simulated. Not modelled: a shared vacuum source and its flow, the leak of an unsealed cup into the others, the frame's flex, peel across a long face, foam or needle area grippers. Treat frame results as a screen, then verify on hardware.

candidates.caveat: Nut runner (approximation): a rigid hex socket with a guide funnel on a lateral float; it engages a hex member by shape. The Studio wrist's roll is its spindle [assumed], at the wrist's speed: a clutch limits the torque to its cap (10 N m, under the wrist's 15 N m) and lets go at the release. The socket's walls are stacked slices so the simulator's contacts are as stiff as steel (a solver artifact). Supported in the Studio: members at least 12 mm tall. Not modelled: a motor, a torque transducer, cross-threading, socket wear, a reaction arm. Simulated, verify on hardware.

finalists.label: Tool change: Button-pusher tool > Suction cup

tool_details.caveat: Suction cup (approximation): a compliant lip of rigid segments on a bellows spring with a limited tilt; the seal is a geometric test (every lip segment touching the face, part material under 13 rays inside the lip) gating a MuJoCo adhesion actuator capped at vacuum x lip area (at most 60 kPa). The lip must touch the face: no pull across a gap. Not modelled: air flow, leak rate, porosity, vacuum build-up time (the vacuum follows the shared close ramp and is cut the control tick the seal is lost), lip material hysteresis, peel dynamics beyond the contact distribution. The lip's friction is the part's. Treat suction results as a screen, then verify on hardware.
